newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIA'S UNITED FRONT PANEL ENDS MEETING.
newsitem.headline: INDIA'S UNITED FRONT PANEL ENDS MEETING.

text.p: A meeting of the decision-making Steering Committee of India's ruling United Front coalition to discuss oil prices has ended, an alliance official said on Wednesday.
The 15-party coalition had been scheduled to consider raising the prices of some petroleum products as part of a plan to rein in the cost of a government subsidy programme.

At the end of 1996/97 (April-March), the government owed 155 billion rupees ($4.3 billion) to state oil companies, which sell some petroleum products such as kerosene to consumers at below-market prices.
The government makes up the difference to the oil companies, but the debt has been mounting rapidly because of the difference between domestic and world prices.
